responses.topThreeActions:
Over the past two years, three actions stand out as especially meaningful in advancing DC Statehood:

1. Elevating Public Awareness Nationwide
I’ve consistently highlighted the case for DC Statehood in discussions, educational content, and civic conversations—helping explain why over 700,000 residents of Washington, D.C. deserve full voting representation in Congress. Increasing general understanding is foundational to building sustained national support.

2. Supporting Legislative Momentum
I’ve helped clarify and communicate the details and significance of the Washington, D.C. Admission Act, including what statehood would mean for representation, budgeting, and local autonomy. Clear explanations help more people engage meaningfully with the policy itself rather than just the politics around it.

3. Centering Democratic Principles
I’ve emphasized the broader constitutional and civil rights arguments—framing DC Statehood as an issue of equal citizenship and democratic fairness. By grounding the conversation in shared democratic values, it strengthens long-term advocacy efforts beyond any single news cycle.
responses.intendedActions:
As a DC elected official, I would focus on five key actions to advance Statehood and protect Home Rule:

1. Push for passage of the Washington, D.C. Admission Act by working closely with the United States Congress. 

2. Defend the District of Columbia Home Rule Act by opposing congressional attempts to overturn locally passed laws.

3. Mobilize residents and national allies to frame Statehood as a civil rights and democracy issue.

4. Protect DC’s budget autonomy to reduce federal interference in locally raised funds.
Prepare operationally for Statehood to ensure a smooth transition when enacted.

DC residents deserve full representation and control over their own laws.
responses.congressResponse:
If elected, I will defend the right of the people of the District of Columbia to govern themselves.

If United States Congress attempts to overturn DC laws or block the budget, I would publicly oppose the action and I would take three specific actions:

1. Formally oppose and lobby against disapproval resolutions in the United States House of Representatives and the United States Senate, organizing a rapid-response coalition to stop them before passage.

2. Pursue legal action by directing the DC Attorney General to challenge any overreach in federal court.

3. Push for permanent reform, including passage of the Washington, D.C. Admission Act and stronger local budget autonomy protections.

My priority would be defending DC’s right to govern itself.
responses.partners: The top partners I plan to engage in promoting DC statehood include my colleagues in the U.S. Senate and House of Representatives, as well as national and local advocacy organizations that have long championed this cause, such as DC Vote and other civic groups. By combining these legislative and grassroots partnerships, I aim to build momentum and foster bipartisan support for the District of Columbia Admission Act (S. 51). I also maintain professional relationships with several congressional staffers whose members support DC statehood, which will help advance these efforts.
responses.voterInvolvement:
To involve D.C. voters and residents in the fight for Statehood, I would focus on three priorities:

1. Educate and Inform
Host ward-based forums explaining how lack of statehood affects taxation, budget control, and representation in the United States Congress. Share clear comparisons showing that states like Wyoming have full representation while D.C. does not.

2. Mobilize Grassroots Action
Build neighborhood-based Statehood Action Teams, partner with local organizations, and work closely with leaders to connect residents directly to federal advocacy efforts.

3. Engage Youth and Community Voices
Activate students at institutions such as Howard University and empower young leaders to drive digital campaigns, rallies, and storytelling initiatives.

The goal is to make statehood personal, visible, and community-led—so residents aren’t just supporting the movement, but shaping it.
responses.additionalComments:
I strongly support DC statehood because the more than 700,000 residents of the District pay federal taxes, serve in the military, and fulfill all the responsibilities of citizenship — yet they lack full voting representation in Congress. That fundamental imbalance contradicts the democratic principles our nation claims to uphold.

For decades, residents of Washington, D.C. have been denied voting representation in the United States Congress, despite having a population larger than several existing states. The rallying cry on DC license plates — “Taxation Without Representation” — is not symbolic; it reflects a real democratic deficit.

Statehood would:
1. Provide two U.S. Senators and at least one voting Representative.
2. Grant full local autonomy over budgeting and laws.
3. Ensure DC residents have equal standing with citizens in all 50 states.

I believe DC statehood is not a partisan issue — it is a fairness issue. If we believe in government by the people, then we must ensure all Americans have an equal voice in that government.

DC voters deserve nothing less than full democracy.

responses.topThreeActions:
Hosted Zoom calls to drive early voter engagement and voter registration to counter the impact of the SAVE Act (if passed by the Senate). I focused these calls on protecting ballot access and preventing disenfranchisement that would weaken our ability in DC and nationally to elect representatives who support DC Statehood and defend Home Rule.

Hosted a series of civic education webinars for HBCU students connecting civic engagement, states’ rights, and DC Statehood. I highlighted why Statehood for DC matters even for people who don’t live in the nation’s capital, because DC’s lack of equal representation is a democracy issue with national consequences.

Built coalition power through my involvement in Win With Black Women. As a member, I support a mission focused on empowering Black women to drive policy, support candidates who back DC Statehood, and build durable, cross-industry relationships that strengthen organizing capacity and sustained advocacy.
responses.intendedActions:
As a DC elected official, I will pursue a “pressure + participation + protection” strategy:

Pressure Congress with organized, timed resident action tied to Congressional calendars, including rapid mobilization when interference bills move and coordinated outreach to key Senate and House targets.

Expand civic education and voter engagement at scale, building on my webinars and Zoom trainings by launching a consistent schedule of Statehood teach-ins, registration and engagement drives, and “how Congress impacts DC” briefings.

Nationalize the DC Statehood case by leveraging cross-state relationships and national networks to make DC Statehood a democracy priority beyond the District, not just a local issue.

Build durable coalitions that center Black women and community leadership, including continuing active engagement with Win With Black Women to support candidates and policies that advance Statehood and defend Home Rule.

Keep DC residents in the driver’s seat through ward-based organizing, transparent updates, and easy-to-use action tools so residents always know: what’s happening, what it means, and what to do next.
responses.congressResponse:
Specific action: I will activate a 24-hour Home Rule Rapid Response that includes a public briefing, coordinated press with coalition partners, and a resident action push targeted at the Members of Congress driving the interference.

That includes:

A district-targeted pressure plan (calls, visits, emails, earned media, and partner mobilization) aimed at the Senate/House decision-makers.

A public “harm receipt” explaining what interference will cost DC residents in real terms (services, public safety, schools, and local economic stability).

Coordination with legal and civil rights partners when appropriate to support challenges and protect DC’s democratic rights.

Congressional interference is not theoretical. Recent federal action to block DC’s local tax changes is one example of how Congress can undercut DC’s autonomy and budget choices.

Free DC
Relationship: Values-aligned partner. I plan to work in active collaboration with Free DC’s organizing and national ally mobilization model to defend Home Rule and advance Statehood.

DC Vote
Relationship: Strategic ally. DC Vote is a long-standing grassroots advocacy organization focused on self-government and full voting rights, and I intend to work closely with them on coordinated advocacy and public education.

ACLU of DC / DC Statehood Now campaign

responses.voterInvolvement:
I will build a resident-led Statehood effort that is consistent, accessible, and measurable:

Ward-based Statehood teams with monthly goals (registration, turnout, outreach, teach-ins, Congressional pressure).

Ongoing civic education, expanding the model I used with HBCU students into a DC-wide program that clearly connects Home Rule, budget autonomy, and representation.

Simple action pathways, including scripts, toolkits, and recurring “Statehood Action Hours” so residents can plug in even with limited time.

Youth and student engagement, treating Statehood as a generational democracy fight, not a niche policy issue.

National ally activation, so DC residents are supported by people across the country who can pressure Members of Congress in their home districts.
responses.additionalComments:
DC Statehood is a civil rights issue and a democracy issue. Home Rule is not enough when Congress can override DC laws and control DC’s budget. The only lasting solution is full Statehood and equal representation.

I also believe the fight for Statehood is inseparable from protecting voting access nationwide. Efforts like the SAVE Act, which would require documentary proof of citizenship to register to vote in federal elections, risk creating barriers that could disenfranchise eligible voters and weaken our ability to elect Statehood champions.

responses.topThreeActions: As a DNC Deputy National Finance Chair, I fought hard to defeat Donald Trump, and to persuade my own Democratic Party to prioritize DC Statehood. As a citizen, I have been active in protests, demonstrations, and education about statehood. And as a Candidate for DC Delegate, I have begun building a strategy to win over leading Democrats, persuadable Republicans, and the people who influence both.
responses.intendedActions: On Day One of every term, I will introduce a Statehood bill in the US House -- as Delegate Norton did. Then I will execute a carefully crafted strategy to win over key Democrats and persuadable Republicans, and I will undergird this strategy with a national marketing campaign to educate Americans everywhere about the injustice and outrage of DC's disenfranchisement. Truly, people don't know, or don't know why they should care.
responses.congressResponse: I will shout our resistance from the rooftops -- but more importantly, I will have recruited allies and partners in advance across Congress to help fight with us and for us.
responses.partners: DC Vote, DC Statehood PAC, Free DC. I am friendly with Board members of the first two, and I have attended many Free DC trainings and events.
responses.voterInvolvement: We need our own education campaign -- too many residents even in DC don't really think about statehood. I'll tie that campaign to America's overall emergence from the Trump nightmare -- once he is gone, America must and WILL rededicate ourselves to the principles of democracy, and I will argue that DC Statehood should be the #1 gesture and symbol of that recommitment.
responses.additionalComments: Let's be clear: if the Republicans thought THEY would get 2 new Senators from making DC a state, we'd have been a state for years. We have to call out this hypocrisy -- and at the same time, find avenues beyond shame (because they have so little); i.e., a grand bargain that gives us statehood and Republicans something they want. As Delegate I will work very hard to find that bargain.

responses.topThreeActions: I have participated in numerous DC statehood actions with groups like Free DC, spoken with and shared my passion for statehood with residents all over the District, and have extensively researched the issue with constitutional lawyers to thoroughly understand the tools available to my administration that will help us execute our Statehood strategy.
responses.intendedActions:
As Mayor, I will make expanding the rights of DC residents a governing priority - not just through the fight for statehood, but by exploring every available avenue to secure representation while that longer fight continues.

Statehood remains the goal. Full statehood is the only complete solution as it gives DC residents congressional voting power. I will sustain that fight with dedicated staff, national advocacy, and coordination with our next Congresswoman and our Shadow delegation. But I will also pursue interim paths to representation.  Specifically, I will work with Congressional allies to revive efforts to secure a voting House member for DC without requiring full statehood. Here's how that could work:

The DC House Voting Rights Act approach: Congress has considered legislation that would grant DC a voting representative in the House by statute. Previous versions (2007, 2009) passed the House but stalled in the Senate. These bills treated DC "as though it were a state" for purposes of House representation, relying on Congress's broad authority under the District Clause (Article I, Section 8, Clause 17). Past versions paired DC's seat with an additional seat for a Republican-leaning state to build bipartisan support. As Mayor, I will actively lobby for renewed Congressional action on this approach.

Critics argue that Article I limits House membership to "the several States," meaning only a constitutional amendment can grant DC a House vote. Supporters counter that the District Clause gives Congress plenary authority over DC, including the power to treat it as a state for specific purposes—as we already do for federal programs, judicial proceedings, and other matters. This is a live legal debate, and I believe DC should force the question rather than accept disenfranchisement as permanent.

A targeted constitutional amendment: If the statutory path faces insurmountable legal challenges, a constitutional amendment focused solely on House representation could be considered. The 23rd Amendment (giving DC electoral votes) passed in 1961 with bipartisan support because it was narrowly tailored. A similar amendment for House representation could potentially attract support from members who aren't ready for full statehood but recognize the injustice of total disenfranchisement.

Statehood is the right answer. But DC residents have been waiting for representation since 1801. As Mayor, I will pursue every constitutionally available path—statutory, legal, and political—to expand our rights while the statehood fight continues. We should not let the perfect be the enemy of progress.
responses.congressResponse:
When Congress attempts to overturn DC laws or block our budget, I will respond with sustained resistance. Political, legal, and organizational.

I will use the visibility of the Mayor's office to publicly oppose every instance of Congressional overreach, making clear to DC residents and the national audience that this is exactly why we need statehood. Congressional interference is taxation without representation happening in real time.

I will expand my DC federal affairs department to ensure that we are talking at all times with all members or the DC subcommittee on both the House and Senate, and have relations with the Speaker and the Majority leader.

I will work with the Council to continue pursuing budget autonomy, building on the 2013 referendum that DC voters approved. Congress's refusal to fully recognize our budget autonomy is itself an argument for statehood.

Where specific Congressional actions violate constitutional rights beyond the District Clause - speech, equal protection, due process - I will coordinate with the Attorney General's office to explore legal challenges.

And I will seek creative implementation approaches that honor DC law and the will of DC voters to the maximum extent possible within federal constraints.
responses.partners:
With Delegate Norton's retirement, DC will elect new representation in Congress this June. As Mayor, I will build a strong working relationship with whoever DC voters choose, ensuring the Mayor's office and the Delegate's office are fully coordinated on statehood advocacy, federal relations, and defending home rule. Given the current federal administration's unprecedented intervention in DC, this partnership is more critical than ever.

I will build a unified statehood coalition. DC has multiple organizations fighting for statehood and home rule—DC Vote, Free DC, 51 for 51, the Statehood Commission, and others. Each does important work, but the advocacy landscape is fragmented. As Mayor, I will work to convene these groups to build a unified coalition with shared messaging, coordinated strategy, and combined resources. The Mayor's office can serve as the convening table that brings these groups together without any single organization having to cede its identity or mission.

And my third “partner” would be the people of DC. We have the resources, the intellectual power, and the passion to build what we need to drive this fight forward.
responses.voterInvolvement:
Statehood cannot be won by elected officials alone. It will require sustained civic engagement from residents. As Mayor, I will:

Integrate statehood education into civic engagement programs, including through initiatives like the Capital Corps, which will train thousands of DC residents in civic participation. The Capital Corps, which is one of my priority initiatives, will create pathways for 5,000 DC residents to serve their communities while earning education credits, job training, and professional certifications. Eight specialized service branches give every Washingtonian a place to serve, a path to grow, and a reason to stay.

I will ensure that efforts to reach statehood have the backing and visibility of the Mayor's office and that we provide support and amplify resident-led advocacy, ensuring that when DC residents organize, lobby, or speak out for statehood.

Make the connection between daily governance and statehood explicit. Every time Congress interferes with our laws, every time we face budget uncertainty, I will communicate clearly to residents: this is why statehood matters to your life.
responses.additionalComments:
DC Statehood is not a partisan issue; it is a democracy issue. 700,000 Americans are denied full representation in Congress. We pay federal taxes, serve in the military, and contribute to the nation, yet we lack the same rights and representation as other states.

As someone who served in the U.S. Army and has built my life in this city, I take the principle of self-determination personally. DC residents deserve the same rights as every other American. As Mayor, I will never stop fighting for statehood. Not as a rhetorical exercise, but as a governing priority.

responses.topThreeActions: I have consistently promoted Statehood in public forums and civic discussions, worked to maintain broad coalitions across civic and political organizations, and defended Home Rule against congressional interference. My support extends over 40 years, including service as National Committeeman and helping secure the District's first-in-the-nation presidential primary in 2000 to elevate DC's national voice and visibility.
responses.intendedActions: I will regularly engage members of Congress and national audiences, coordinate a unified District response with local leadership, and support legislation and resolutions asserting District authority. I will also build interstate and national alliances so Statehood is recognized as a civil rights issue affecting American democracy, not solely a local matter.
responses.congressResponse: I will proactively meet with Congress when legislation may draw scrutiny, coordinate District leadership to present a unified position, and formally oppose interference. I will personally advocate on Capitol Hill to defeat disapproval measures and keep residents informed and engaged so Congress understands the real impact of its actions.
responses.partners: I will work with District leadership, business and civic organizations such as the Federal City Council, DC Chamber of Commerce, and Board of Trade, and community organizations across all eight wards. My longstanding relationships with these groups help build a broad coalition demonstrating that Statehood benefits residents, institutions, and local economy.
responses.voterInvolvement: I will hold community forums and town halls, partner with civic associations and schools, and organize coordinated advocacy so Congress hears directly from District voters. Ongoing public education and participation will be central to advancing Statehood.
responses.additionalComments: Statehood is a fundamental civil rights issue affecting more than 700,000 residents. I have supported it for over four decades and will continue advocating for equal representation and protection of Home Rule until Statehood is achieved.

responses.topThreeActions:
However, I can share the three ways I have most effectively supported the discourse on statehood (such as for Washington D.C. or Puerto Rico) for over the last two years. My "pride" comes from providing objective, high-quality information that helps people understand complex constitutional issues. 

1. Synthesizing Complex Legal Arguments
The debate over statehood involves intricate constitutional law, specifically regarding the Admissions Clause and the District Clause. 
What I’ve done: I have researched on the hundreds breaking down the "Tennessee Plan" (a historical strategy for statehood) and explain how it might apply to modern territories.
The Impact: This turns dense legal theories into accessible knowledge, allowing to engage in the debate with a firmer grasp of the precedent. 

2. Providing Non-Partisan Comparative Analysis
Statehood is often viewed through a purely political lens. I focus on providing a balanced view of the pros and cons across different dimensions: 
Economic: Analyzing federal funding shifts vs. local tax autonomy.
Political: Explaining the potential impact on the Electoral College and Congressional balance.
Civil: Highlighting the arguments regarding voting representation and self-determination. 

3. Creating Educational Frameworks
I have research educators and students in creating structured debates and research papers on the topic.
What I’ve done: I studied and researched comprehensive bibliographies, summarize historical referendums (like those in Puerto Rico in 2012, 2017, and 2020), and outline the legislative hurdles currently facing bills like H.R. 51.
The Impact: This ensures that the next generation of voters understands the mechanics of how the Union actually grows and changes.
responses.intendedActions:
I, Michael "The Enforcer" Graham, a former Georgetown Hoya basketball champion, has centered my campaign on "giving the people back their city". While his primary focus has been on affordability for youth and seniors, his candidacy is framed as a defense of community empowerment against outside influence. 

Community Advocacy: He emphasizes using his "Enforcer" reputation to fight for local control and ensure D.C. residents have a primary voice in their city's future.
Grassroots Mobilization: His campaign utilizes grassroots activities to engage voters directly on issues of local sovereignty and economic stability. 
Specific Actions to Promote D.C. Statehood

D.C. leaders are taking the following legislative and advocacy steps in 2025 and 2026:
The Washington, D.C. Admission Act (H.R. 51): Reintroducing and championing this bill to admit the residential areas of D.C. as the 51st state (the Douglass Commonwealth) while maintaining a smaller federal district for government buildings.

D.C. Statehood Pledge: Mobilizing candidates and elected officials to sign the D.C. Statehood Pledge, committing to the formal admission of D.C. into the Union.
National Education Campaigns: Using the upcoming U.S. 250th anniversary in 2026 as a platform to highlight the lack of voting representation for D.C.’s 700,000 residents. 
Protecting Home Rule from Federal Interference

In response to "attacks on limited Home Rule" in 2025 and early 2026, officials are focused on:
The District of Columbia Legislative Home Rule Act: Supporting federal legislation (like H.R. 214) designed to eliminate Congress's authority to nullify locally enacted D.C. laws.
Defending Local Prosecution Power: Opposing efforts to strip the D.C. Attorney General of power and fighting for the transfer of local prosecution authority from the federal U.S. Attorney’s Office to local control.

Police and Guard Autonomy: Advocating for the repeal of Section 740 of the Home Rule Act, which allows the President to seize control of the Metropolitan Police Department during "emergencies," and seeking mayoral control over the D.C. National Guard.
responses.congressResponse:
As a candidate for the D.C. Council in 2026, I Michael Graham has positioned myself as a community-first advocate who intends to lead aggressive grassroots and legislative defenses against federal interference. 
If elected, I will response to congressional attempts to overturn D.C. laws or block the budget would center on the following specific actions:

1. Direct Grassroots Mobilization and Civil Resistance
Michael Graham, known as "The Enforcer," has stated that his primary response to federal overreach will be activating the community for direct action.
Specific Action: Graham intends to organize and lead large-scale "rapid-response" grassroots demonstrations across the city to physically and politically protest congressional interference.
Goal: He views his role as a "liberation fighter" who uses public pressure to make the political cost of overturning local D.C. laws too high for members of Congress to ignore. 

2. Legal Challenges to the Home Rule Act
In 2026, the D.C. government faces renewed threats to its autonomy. Graham plans to utilize the Council’s legal standing to challenge federal mandates.
Specific Action: He supports filing injunctions and lawsuits against federal attempts to seize control of local functions—such as the Metropolitan Police Department or the local budget—arguing that such moves violate the spirit of the 1973 Home Rule Act.
Judicial Advocacy: He would push for the Council to formally demand that the federal government fill local judicial vacancies with the District's recommended nominees to ensure the local court system remains independent of federal political agendas. 

3. Legislative Decoupling of the Budget
To prevent the federal government from "starving" D.C. services through budget riders, Graham supports structural changes to how the city manages its finances.
Specific Action: He advocates for the Council to work with Delegate Eleanor Holmes Norton to pass legislation that would make the D.C. local budget financially independent and distinct from the U.S. federal budget process.
Fiscal Autonomy: This would involve a strategy where local tax dollars are managed under a separate authority that does not require an annual affirmative act of Congress to be spent. 

4. Expanding the National Statehood Platform
Graham intends to use D.C.’s status in 2026—the year of the U.S. 250th anniversary—to frame congressional interference as a national civil rights crisis.
Specific Action: He plans to launch an educational grant program through the Council to inform the national public about the lack of voting representation in D.C., using the "DC250" celebrations to lobby for the admission of D.C. as the 51st state.
responses.partners:
As a candidate for the D.C. Council At-Large seat in 2026, Michael Graham has identified key strategic partners whose collaboration is essential to his mission of achieving statehood and safeguarding local autonomy.

1. D.C. Statehood Delegation (Shadow Senators and Representative) 
Graham views the District's elected "Shadow" delegation as the primary frontline in the legislative battle for statehood.
The Partnership: If elected, Graham intends to coordinate directly with the Shadow Senators and Representative to align Council-led grassroots mobilization with federal legislative strategy.
Current Relationship: Graham is a signatory of the D.C. Statehood Pledge, which formally aligns his campaign with the goals of the Shadow Delegation and other statehood-focused candidates. He maintains a communicative relationship with current and aspiring delegation members to ensure a unified front in 2026. 

2. 100 Black Men of America, Inc. 
As a long-standing leader within this organization, Graham intends to leverage its national network to broaden the D.C. statehood movement into a national civil rights issue.
The Partnership: He plans to utilize the organization’s reach to educate communities outside the District about the lack of voting representation, treating statehood as a fundamental issue of democratic equality.
Current Relationship: Graham has been a founding member of the Prince George's County chapter since 2012 and serves as the National Chairman of the Communications and Public Relations Committee. This deep-rooted leadership role provides him with a powerful platform to amplify D.C.'s message nationally. 

3. Progressive Advocacy Groups (e.g., DC for Democracy)
To combat congressional attempts to overturn local laws, Graham intends to work closely with local activist organizations that can mobilize "rapid-response" resistance.
The Partnership: These partners would be responsible for the ground-level execution of the grassroots demonstrations Graham plans to lead when Home Rule is threatened.
Current Relationship: Graham is actively engaging with these groups during the 2026 campaign cycle. For instance, he participated in the DC for Democracy candidate forums, demonstrating an ongoing dialogue with the city's most active progressive organizers.
responses.voterInvolvement:
I, Michael Graham, as a 2026 candidate for the DC Council, intends to involve voters and residents through a strategy centered on grassroots mobilization, national coalition-building, and high-visibility public education. His approach emphasizes transforming statehood from a local legislative goal into an active community movement.

1. Direct Community Mobilization & "Rapid Response"
Graham plans to turn residents into "liberation fighters" to defend local sovereignty. 
Mass Demonstrations: He intends to organize and lead large-scale community protests to physically and politically challenge any congressional attempts to overturn local laws or block the D.C. budget.
Voter Empowerment: His campaign is built on the philosophy of "giving the people back their city," focusing on empowering neighborhood groups to act as the primary defense against federal overreach. 

2. National Advocacy & Strategic Partnerships
Graham intends to use his national leadership roles to connect D.C. residents with allies across the United States.
100 Black Men of America: Leveraging his role as a national leader in this organization, he plans to involve D.C. residents in national education campaigns that frame statehood as a fundamental civil rights and democratic equality issue.
DC Statehood PAC: As a co-chair, he urges residents to join organized efforts to identify and support pro-statehood candidates in congressional races nationwide, helping D.C. voters influence the makeup of the body that currently governs them. 

3. Civic Education & Public Awareness
To sustain long-term engagement, Graham focuses on increasing the "civic literacy" of the District.

The DC250 Initiative: He plans to use the U.S. 250th anniversary in 2026 to host town halls, exhibits, and educational grants that highlight D.C.'s 200-year struggle for representation.
Interactive Toolkits: He supports providing residents with structured toolkits—similar to those from the Official DC Statehood Site—to help them lobby members of Congress directly and participate in "Statehood Day" activities.

responses.additionalComments:
Michael Graham, as a candidate for the D.C. Council in 2026  has emphasized that the quest for statehood is currently in "great danger" due to increased federal attacks on local autonomy. 

He wishes to share the following core beliefs and calls to action with D.C. voters:
1. Rejection of the "Patronage Plantation System"
Graham strongly opposes any return to the era before the 1973 Home Rule Act, when D.C. was governed by unelected representatives. 
The Vision: He views the current federal oversight as a "colonizing" force and believes that full statehood is the only way to achieve "Full Self Determination".
The Struggle: He frames the fight for statehood as a modern liberation movement, calling residents to act as "DC Liberation Fighters" to protect the District's limited sovereignty. 

2. Strategic National Political Engagement
Graham believes the path to statehood requires D.C. voters to influence national politics beyond the District's borders.
Targeting Federal Enemies: He advocates for identifying "enemies" of D.C. statehood in Congress and actively working to remove them through political organizing.
Seating National Allies: Conversely, he urges residents to help seat pro-statehood allies across the U.S. to build a legislative majority capable of passing admission acts like H.R. 51. 

3. Immediate Defense of Home Rule
While statehood is the long-term goal, Graham insists that protecting Home Rule is the immediate priority for 2026. 
Local Control of Funds: He warns that federal attempts to seize control of D.C. tax dollars and law enforcement are direct threats to the city's future.
Collective Action: He urges voters to support the DC Statehood PAC to provide the financial and organizational infrastructure needed to "fight back" against these federal incursions.

responses.topThreeActions:
1.	Oye used the role of DC’s U.S. Representative to organize nationally for DC statehood. Oye has coordinated with national civil rights leaders, labor unions, and elected officials across the country to elevate DC statehood through advocacy days, coalition letters, public testimony, and national media.
	2.	Oye has publicly opposed congressional and executive interference in DC’s self-government. Over the past two years, Oye has consistently spoken out—locally and nationally—against congressional overrides, budget interference, and federal actions that undermine home rule, including renewed Trump-era attacks on DC laws, funding, and autonomy. This has also included standing up for voter-approved initiatives when local government leaders moved to overturn the will of DC residents.
	3.	Oye has defended DC residents and immigrant communities harmed by non-statehood. Oye has used his office and public platform to call out ICE overreach, family separations, and federal enforcement abuses that DC is uniquely vulnerable to because it lacks statehood. He has directly linked these harms to disenfranchisement, making clear that statehood is essential to protecting families, workers, and civil liberties in the District.
responses.intendedActions: As a DC Councilmember, Oye will continue building broad coalitions locally and nationally to advance DC statehood and defend home rule. He will use the Council seat to educate residents and national partners, oppose congressional interference, and protect voter-approved ballot initiatives from being overturned. Oye will build on existing momentum to ensure DC laws, budgets, and democratic decisions are respected and defended.
responses.congressResponse: When Congress attempts to overturn DC laws or block the District’s budget, Oye will use every available tool to defend home rule. He will support further decoupling DC policy from federal control — including tax and administrative systems — and use the Council’s platform to organize public pressure, direct action, and coordinated noncompliance when appropriate. Protecting DC’s autonomy requires both legislative strategy and visible, collective resistance.
responses.partners:
We will work with our current endorsing partners - DC Voters for Animals, Working Families Party, Unite Here Local 25, LiUNA, Ghana PAC, 314 Action, and the Nigerian-American PAC to advance statehood. 

We also hope to earn endorsements from Free DC and DC for Democracy. We have worked with both organizations to advance statehood, you can read more here: https://www.axios.com/local/washington-dc/2026/01/15/dc-council-trump-shadow-representative-senator-election
responses.voterInvolvement: Oye will continue engaging DC residents directly through rallies, community events, door-to-door outreach, and public education on statehood. He has organized and participated in lobby days, national advocacy efforts, and local actions that use DC’s proximity to federal power to demand equal rights. As a Councilmember, he will keep residents at the center of the statehood fight by making it visible, accessible, and action-oriented.
responses.additionalComments: DC statehood is about survival, dignity, and self-determination. The ongoing denial of statehood creates real harm, from budget instability to federal overreach and family separation, and our response must match the urgency of those conditions. Oye believes it is time to raise the stakes, confront these injustices directly, and fight for full democracy with the seriousness DC residents deserve.

responses.topThreeActions:
We are witnessing nothing short of an assault on DC's democracy and autonomy. These actions are completely unacceptable, unnecessary, costly, and unconstitutional. They represent creeping fascism that threatens not just DC residents' ability to govern ourselves, but the safety, dignity, and fundamental rights of our most vulnerable neighbors—particularly our immigrant communities who are being terrorized by ICE raids and deportations.

As an ANC1E Commissioner I voted consistently in support of Statehood and in opposition to federal overreach. That included (1) opposition to Congressional interference with 16 bills to roll back DC laws and (2) support for the swift adoption of the DC budget without Congressional interference as well as (3) resolutions affirming Sanctuary City status. On a personal note, joining Statehood actions with Free DC has been a particularly meaningful way to be in community with other Ward 1 residents.
responses.intendedActions:
The role of Councilmembers in resisting this federal overreach is not passive—it requires bold, strategic, and relentless action. As Ward 1 Councilmember, I will approach this fight on multiple fronts:
First and most importantly, I will continue standing and speaking out against Trump and federal interference at every opportunity and publicly denouncing his actions. While silence can be viewed as strategic, I see it as complicity. DC residents deserve a Councilmember who will name what we're facing: fascism, white supremacy, and authoritarian federal overreach that treats DC residents as second-class citizens without full democratic rights. I will use my platform to make clear that these actions are attacks not just on local autonomy but on the fundamental principles of democracy and self-governance. As Councilmember, I do not support our community being terrorized and will use fierce resistance and my legislative powers and organizing skills to fight back!

Second, I will use the Council's legislative powers to close loopholes in local law that allow for inappropriate cooperation with federal authorities like ICE. DC has declared itself a sanctuary city, but that commitment means nothing if local agencies and resources are being used to facilitate deportations and immigration enforcement. I will introduce or co-sponsor legislation that: explicitly prohibits DC government employees and agencies from cooperating with ICE except where absolutely required by law; prevents the use of DC resources, facilities, or personnel to support federal immigration enforcement; strengthens protections for sensitive locations like schools, hospitals, and places of worship; and creates penalties for violations of these policies. 

Third, I will use the Council's oversight and investigative powers to document federal overreach and hold hearings that expose the human cost of these attacks. I will demand that DC agencies report on every instance of federal interference: How many times has ICE requested cooperation? How are federal deployments of the National Guard affecting public safety and community trust? What is the fiscal impact of blocked budget funds on critical services? What legal violations are occurring? These hearings will serve multiple purposes: creating a public record of federal abuses, amplifying the voices of residents directly harmed, building political pressure for resistance, and identifying specific areas where local action is needed. I will invite legal experts, immigrant rights advocates, constitutional scholars, and most importantly, DC residents experiencing this persecution to testify and share their stories.

Fourth, I will advocate for dedicating DC government resources to legal challenges against unconstitutional federal actions. The Office of the Attorney General should be filing lawsuits challenging every significant federal overreach—from budget blocks to forced cooperation with immigration enforcement to violations of the Home Rule Act. I will use my budget powers to ensure the OAG has adequate resources for this litigation.  Attorney General Brian Schwalb has already filed multiple lawsuits challenging Trump administration overreach, including suits against the attempted federal takeover of MPD and the deployment of National Guard troops in the District, which he has described as an illegal "military occupation." His office has argued that these federal actions violate the Home Rule Act and represent "the gravest threat to Home Rule that the District has ever faced." As Councilmember, I will ensure that the OAG has robust budget allocations to continue and expand this critical litigation, recognizing that legal challenges are one of our most powerful tools for protecting DC autonomy. I will also use my oversight powers to publicly support AG Schwalb's efforts, amplify the cases he's bringing, and pressure the Mayor and other agencies to fully cooperate with legal strategies to resist federal overreach. The Attorney General cannot fight these battles alone—he needs the full backing of the Council, adequate resources, and coordinated action across DC government.
 
Fifth, I will work to ensure that DC government actively protects residents rather than passively allowing federal persecution. This means: creating emergency funds to support residents facing deportation or federal prosecution; ensuring that DC's identification programs remain accessible to all residents regardless of immigration status; maintaining and expanding language access so that non-English speakers can access services and know their rights; and using every available tool in local government to create barriers to federal enforcement and sanctuaries for vulnerable residents. Because Ward 1 has the highest concentration of immigrant residents in the city, I will leverage my Council position to ensure that our non-profit organizations who protect and serve our immigrant neighbors are well-resourced and represented by their elected officials. We should have their back and demonstrate that with our legislative and budgetary power and authorities!
responses.congressResponse: I will work directly with Members of Congress who support DC statehood and autonomy to build federal legislative strategies to protect our self-governance. While we cannot rely on Congress to save us—particularly under Republican control—we must maintain relationships with allies who can introduce legislation, use committee hearings to expose abuses, and build public pressure. My seven years as a registered federal lobbyist gave me experience navigating Capitol Hill, building relationships with congressional staff, and understanding how to influence federal policy even from disadvantaged positions. I will leverage these skills to advocate for DC autonomy, budget release, and legislative protections against federal overreach.
responses.partners: I will partner with legal clinics and nonprofit organizations with experience in organizing campaigns to mobilize, educate, and train DC residents to know their rights and protect themselves from lack of due process and harm. This includes: funding and promoting know-your-rights trainings, particularly for immigrant communities; supporting legal defense funds and rapid response networks that can intervene when ICE conducts raids; ensuring that DC residents understand their Fourth Amendment protections against unreasonable searches and seizures; and building community defense networks where neighbors look out for each other. My decade of community organizing through Georgia Avenue Thrive taught me that residents with knowledge and collective power can resist even well-resourced oppression. We must build infrastructure that allows our community to protect itself, not wait for government institutions to save us.
responses.voterInvolvement: As a Ward 1 resident for over 20 years and ANC Commissioner for a decade, I've walked these streets not as a policymaker observing from afar, but as a neighbor, a community organizer, and someone deeply invested in the safety and well-being of every person who calls our ward home. I co-founded and led what is now Georgia Avenue Thrive—a community led initiative evolving from a public safety taskforce that brought together residents, small businesses, and local government to address safety concerns not through increased policing, but through community activation, economic development, and collaborative problem-solving. I've seen firsthand that real community comes from investment in people and neighborhoods. DC is under attack by President Trump and Congress right now, and now is the time to come together and fight together.
responses.additionalComments:
As a candidate for DC Council in Ward 1, I am deeply alarmed by what we are witnessing — not just here in DC, but in cities across this country. We are watching democratic norms erode in real time. We are seeing the will of voters undermined, local decision-making attacked, and power consolidated in ways that silence communities instead of uplifting them.

And I’m angry.

I’m angry because the people who bear the brunt of democratic backsliding are Black and Brown residents — the very communities who have fought hardest to expand access to the ballot, to housing, to safety, to education, to opportunity. In DC, a majority-Black city with no full voting representation in Congress, our lack of statehood is not an accident. It is the result of unbalanced power rooted in structural racism — a system that has long been comfortable controlling Black political power while denying Black political self-determination.

When local decisions are overridden, when budgets are interfered with, when our autonomy is treated as conditional, it sends a clear message: our democracy is fragile, and it is not distributed equally.

We cannot separate today’s democracy crisis from white supremacy. White supremacy is not just about hate; it is about power — who holds it, who protects it, and who is denied it. Structural racism has shaped whose voices are centered and whose are dismissed. And when democracy weakens, those already pushed to the margins are the first to feel the impact.

What we are dealing with today isn’t new. It has always existed in different forms — voter suppression, disenfranchisement, redlining, over-policing, economic exclusion. What’s different is the face it wears and the boldness with which it operates at a time when we should be progressing, not moving backwards as we are today.
But history also teaches us something else: when democracy is threatened, people organize. People build. People fight forward.
It’s time to level the playing field so all people can win. It’s time to strengthen local power, protect our rights, fight for statehood and ensure that DC residents have full voice and representation.

Let’s free DC. 

Thank you for your consideration!

responses.intendedActions: Every day on the Council requires navigating these issues.  Challenges arise constantly.  I will participate in strategic lobbying and outreach to the Hill.  And, I expect to be very active in support of pro-Statehood candidates in the upcoming midterm elections.

responses.additionalComments: I am deeply committed to achieving Statehood.  Fundamentally, I think the path is for Democrats to secure control of the House, Senate and Presidency.  Republicans will never allow Statehood to happen if they can block it.  Democrats have had two opportunities, once under Clinton and again under Obama to pass Statehood.  In both cases, our leaders declined to move because they believed Republicans would never work with them if they pushed it through.  And then the Republicans declined to work with them anyways.  We need to win Democratic control and persuade all Democrats that failure to push through Statehood would be wrong, and foolish.

responses.topThreeActions:
1. I have been an active member of the Free DC movement and other local efforts to defend Home Rule and advance DC Statehood, including public demonstrations, press conferences, lobby days, coalition calls, and organizing meetings.

2. Joined the board of DC Statehood PAC to advance our federal fight for self-determination, directing funds to congressional candidates in support of the Washington DC Admission Act.

3. Been an effective spokesperson to media, helping to shape the local and national narrative in the midst of attacks on DC's Home Rule under both the Biden and Trump administrations.
responses.intendedActions:
1. I will use the full platform of the office to keep DC Statehood at the center of the national conversation by building and maintaining a bipartisan congressional coalition, working with state legislators across the country to pass supportive resolutions, and partnering with civil rights, labor, democracy, and good-government organizations to elevate statehood as a national democracy issue. Statehood must be framed not as a local preference, but as unfinished civil rights work and a critical democratic reform.

2. I will actively monitor and respond to congressional riders and oversight efforts that threaten DC’s autonomy. That means coordinated rapid response with the Mayor, Council, Delegate, and regional allies; direct engagement with appropriators; public testimony; and national media advocacy to raise the political cost of federal interference. Congress should not be able to quietly undermine DC’s locally enacted laws.

3. I will treat every major federal debate, from voting rights to reproductive freedom to criminal justice, as connected to DC’s fight. As long as 700,000 residents lack full representation, our democracy remains incomplete.
responses.congressResponse:
If Congress attempts to overturn DC laws or block the District’s budget, I will respond immediately, publicly, and in coordination with every available ally because congressional interference is not just a policy disagreement, it is a denial of democratic self-governance for 700,000 residents.

One specific action I would take is to organize and lead a coordinated federal advocacy push targeting key appropriators and leadership offices the moment a rider or disapproval resolution is introduced. That means direct meetings with members of Congress, mobilizing national civil rights and democracy organizations to apply pressure, and ensuring the issue receives sustained national media attention. Congressional interference often succeeds quietly — I intend to raise the political cost of interference.

I would also work closely with the Mayor, Council, the District’s Delegate to Congress, and my delegation colleagues to present a unified front. When appropriate, I would support litigation strategies to challenge overreach.

Above all, I would make clear that every attempt to override DC law strengthens the moral and political case for Statehood. If Congress insists on governing a city whose residents it does not represent, then it must be prepared to defend that position in full public view.
responses.partners:
Concerned DC Residents and Statehood Advocates: DC residents are the heart of the Statehood movement. As a lifelong Washingtonian, former elected official, and Ward 8 community leader, I have organized alongside neighbors, testified with advocates, and worked in coalition spaces where Statehood has long been a core demand. My relationship with residents and grassroots advocates is not transactional — it’s rooted in shared lived experience. As Senator, I would treat you as essential partners in strategy, mobilization, and movement-building.

National Pro-Democracy Organizations: National pro-democracy and civil rights organizations are essential to framing DC Statehood as a structural democracy issue. In my current role as National Political Director at People For the American Way, I work closely with allied organizations across the country to defend voting rights, civil liberties, and representative government. Those relationships position me to quickly align national messaging, research, grassroots organizing, and federal advocacy efforts around the urgency of Statehood.

Elected Leaders on Capitol Hill and Around the Nation: Building the legislative coalition for Statehood requires sustained engagement with members of Congress and state leaders nationwide. Through my work in national politics and my service as a DC elected official, I have developed relationships with progressive lawmakers, staff, and policy advocates across the country. As Shadow Senator, I would leverage those connections to grow co-sponsors, coordinate public support, and ensure that DC Statehood remains a live and active priority within the broader pro-democracy agenda.
responses.voterInvolvement:
Statehood will not be won solely through congressional maneuvering — it will be won through organized, sustained pressure from DC residents themselves.

1. I will treat the office as an organizing platform, not just an advocacy role. That means hosting regular town halls, ward-based forums, and issue briefings that connect statehood directly to the everyday concerns of residents — housing costs, public safety, reproductive freedom, transportation funding, and protection from federal interference. When people see how lack of representation affects their daily lives, the fight becomes personal and urgent.

2. I will help build and maintain a citywide Statehood coalition that includes civic associations, faith leaders, labor unions, small business owners, students, and neighborhood groups. My goal is to make Statehood visible in every ward — through coordinated days of action, voter education drives, and partnerships with local institutions. We cannot allow Statehood to feel abstract or episodic; it must be woven into the civic culture of the District.

3. I will prioritize youth engagement. Young Washingtonians have often led the moral charge for democracy in this country. By investing in civic education, leadership development, and direct organizing opportunities, we can build the next generation of Statehood advocates who see this as their unfinished work.

4. I will ensure transparency and accountability. Residents deserve regular updates on federal strategy, congressional engagement, and progress. Statehood is a collective effort — and DC voters should feel not like spectators, but like co-authors of the movement that finally secures full representation.
responses.additionalComments:
DC Statehood is not a new position for me, it is the throughline of my public life.

As a student in DC Public Schools, I came to understand early that the decisions shaping my education, my neighborhood, and my future were influenced by members of Congress I could not vote for. That realization didn’t make me cynical. It made me organize. From my earliest days as a youth advocate and student activist, I saw Statehood not as an abstract constitutional debate, but as a question of dignity and equal citizenship.

As an elected member of the DC State Board of Education, I experienced firsthand how vulnerable our local decisions can be to federal interference. And as a national political organizer working to defend democracy across the country, I’ve seen how deeply Americans value representation and self-determination — except, too often, when it comes to the people of their own capital city.

My stance is simple and unwavering: DC deserves full Statehood, full representation, and full control over its budget and laws. Not as a favor. Not as a bargaining chip. But as a matter of fundamental democratic principle.

I am running to be DC’s last Shadow Senator — to help close this chapter in our history and ensure that the next generation of Washingtonians grows up not fighting for equality, but living it.

responses.topThreeActions: As Executive Director of Barracks Row Main Street and Former ANC Commissioner and Chair of ANC 6B, I have spent years working closely with small businesses, community partners, and local leaders to make Capitol Hill and the wider District stronger and more vibrant. These experiences have given me firsthand insight into both the challenges we face—like small business recovery, housing, and equity—and the opportunities we have when we come together. I had the opportunity to talk with US House Members on both Democrat and Republican about DC issues. They were received positively with continued dialogue on the issues. I have also work with national organizations such as the National Restaurant Association and Main Street American on the important of Statehood.
responses.intendedActions:
As U.S. Shadow Representative, I will take an aggressive and relationship-driven approach to advancing DC Statehood and protecting Home Rule.

First, I will commit to meeting with every single Member of the U.S. House of Representatives at least once during my first term. Building direct relationships across the aisle is essential. I will engage members from both parties to identify common ground—whether it’s taxation, military service, public safety, economic fairness, or democratic principles—and connect those issues back to DC’s lack of full representation.

Second, I will prioritize ongoing conversations with Members of Congress and their staff to ensure DC’s interests are consistently represented. Statehood cannot be a one-time ask; it requires sustained engagement and coalition building.

Third, I will work beyond Capitol Hill by engaging Democratic Parties in other states and encouraging them to include DC Statehood in their platforms. I will ask state and local party leaders to actively advocate with their own Representatives and Senators in support of DC’s full voting rights.

Finally, I will expand national education efforts so that DC Statehood becomes a mainstream American issue—not just a local one. I will pursue opportunities to elevate the cause at major national events, such as the Rose Bowl Parade and the Macy’s Thanksgiving Parade, and other large-scale civic gatherings. Millions of Americans tune into these moments. We must use them to tell DC’s story and build public understanding that more than 700,000 taxpaying Americans deserve full representation.
responses.congressResponse:
First, I will organize a coordinated advocacy campaign targeting key Members of Congress, including direct meetings, constituent pressure, and media engagement to oppose the interference. I will work with the Mayor, Council, and national partners to ensure Members understand both the local impact and the broader democratic implications of their actions.

Second, I will hold a press conference and national media briefings to frame the issue clearly: Congressional interference in DC’s local governance is taxation without representation. Elevating the issue nationally is critical to increasing political cost for those attempting to override Home Rule.

Third, I will push for legislative remedies by urging supportive Members of Congress to introduce or reintroduce measures that protect DC’s budget autonomy and limit Congressional micromanagement of local laws.
responses.partners:
First, I intend to work closely with Main Street America. As someone deeply engaged in Main Street corridor revitalization efforts, I understand the power of their national network of local business districts and community development organizations. Main Street America represents communities across the country that believe in local control, economic vitality, and grassroots leadership—values directly aligned with DC’s fight for self-governance.

Second, I plan to partner with the National Restaurant Association. DC’s restaurant industry is a cornerstone of our local economy, and the Association represents thousands of businesses nationwide. Many Members of Congress prioritize restaurant and hospitality issues. I will work to connect the economic strength of DC’s food and beverage sector to the broader argument that the workers and business owners fueling our capital city deserve full representation.

Third, I intend to engage the National Retail Federation. Retailers understand the importance of stable governance, economic predictability, and fair taxation. DC businesses generate billions in economic activity while lacking voting representation in Congress. I will work to elevate that economic fairness argument within the retail community and encourage their advocacy networks to support Statehood.

Today, my relationships with these organizations stem from my work in business corridor revitalization, economic development, and engagement with the restaurant and retail sectors. As Shadow Representative, I will formalize and deepen those partnerships to ensure Statehood is not just a political issue, but a national economic fairness issue.
responses.voterInvolvement: As U.S. Shadow Representative, I would take an aggressive and relationship-driven approach to advancing DC Statehood and protecting Home Rule. First, I would host quarterly "Day on the Hill" lobbying events for statehood and also host events with congressmen to discuss statehood with DC residents.
responses.additionalComments: I am committed to fighting for DC statehood, ensuring every resident has full representation and equal funding. I will champion small businesses, advocating for policies that help our local restaurants, shops, and entrepreneurs thrive. And I will work to build stronger, more equitable communities by supporting affordable housing, cultural programs, and opportunities that reflect the diversity of our city. Together, we can create a fairer, more vibrant future for all Washingtonians.

responses.topThreeActions: Marching for Statehood with Mayor Bowser; volunteering with DC Vote demanding action from Congress; and working with Congresswoman Norton's office to promote Statehood.
responses.intendedActions: Demand that our delegate becomes a representative with voting rights; demand that a constitutional amendment be introduced in Congress that States would vote on to make DC a U.S. State; and demand that DC controls its own financial affairs.
responses.congressResponse: If elected, I would meet with Members of Congress to let them know that blocking DC's budget is not good governance, and eventually would protest these attempts.
responses.partners: DC Vote; and future Congressman Robert White. I've volunteered with DC Vote in the past, and worked with Councilmember White's office on various issues in the past.
responses.voterInvolvement: By informing them of the importance of Statehood through my council actions; via social media posts; and asking DC voters to join me in the fight.
responses.additionalComments: I've been a long-time supporter of DC Statehood. I support our lone member of Congress having voting rights in the House of Representatives, and will do everything in my power to secure DC Statehood for DC residents, if elected to the DC Council.

responses.topThreeActions:
Elevating the National Civil Rights Mandate: I am proud to have drafted and secured a national resolution within the NAACP to reaffirm support for DC Statehood as a fundamental Democratic Right to Self-Determination. This moved the conversation from a local political issue to a national civil rights imperative. (https://naacp.org/resources/naacp-reaffirms-support-statehood-and-democratic-right-self-determination-people-district)

Strategic National Education: I have educated elected officials across the country on how their states' influence over our local budget and laws undermines the heartbeat of our nation. By engaging in a non-partisan capacity, I have helped candidates integrate DC Statehood into their own policy platforms.

Operational Readiness Advocacy: I have championed the transition of DC from a municipal mindset to a "state-ready" framework within the good democracy ecosystem, highlighting that our lack of a vote directly impacts our residents' ability to manage their own local taxes and safety.
responses.intendedActions: I will develop pragmatic legislation and roadmaps to decouple municipal functions from federal control. Aligning home rule with budget autonomy. I will continue to collaborate with civic organizations and administrative bodies to build a nationwide network of voters who will pressure their own representatives to support DC’s rights. Strengthening our administrative presence in civic planning and within the community to ensure that as we grow, our infrastructure is built to state-level standards.
responses.congressResponse: It's important to note that historically we've been reactive to congressional overreach, we should plan to operate on the offense. This could look like a Statehood Readiness and Charter Reform Act to work across the aisle with national allies, the growing crowd of litigious non profit organizations and civic organization making it politically and legally expensive for congress to interfere in our local affairs.
responses.partners:
NAACP DC and National: Working with the NAACP DC to secure a national resolution. I will continue my work with their 2,300 branches to mobilize local communities to demand their legislators respect the democratic rights and the autonomy of DC residents.

Emerge & Forward Party: I have deep connections with these organizations. I will leverage these networks to educate the next generation of leaders to view DC Statehood as a non-negotiable plank in any modern policy platform.
responses.voterInvolvement: It is important to humanize the impact...Clearly communicate how specific instances of congressional overreach affect daily life, from school funding to local safety and how statehood would have mitigated those issues. I love data! it's important to equip residents with the data, DC pays more in federal taxes per capita than any other state and has a larger population than both Vermont and Wyoming. I also believe it's important to modernize the argument against DC Statehood... We will workshop responses to hyper-partisan talking points, reminding the country that the Framers of the constitution could not have foreseen a modern, decentralized society where 700,000+ Americans are structurally excluded out of representation.
responses.additionalComments: I want to commend the generations of advocates who have carried this torch. However, the game is evolving, and we must move with it. In a 2026 reality of remote work and decentralized government, the "federal enclave" is a specific footprint not an entire population of 700,000. I am an independent thinker, researcher and a people centric advocate who views statehood as modernization full stop. We are not asking for a favor; we are demanding the return of the rights we already pay more than ever one else for. It is time to align our 18th-century governing documents with our 21st-century reality.
